label: Case Fatality Rate (2026 BDBV)
source: ECDC Ebola outbreak tracker — data as of 23 September 2026 (published 25 September)
contestNote: Crude national CFR calculated from reported confirmed cases/deaths; DRC's overall CFR has climbed from roughly 20% in early June to a peak near 48.6% in late August and stood at roughly 48.2% as of 23 September (7,890 cases / 3,799 deaths) — essentially flat versus the 21 September report despite the continued rise in absolute numbers. Province-level variation remains stark: North Kivu case growth has surged 73% over the three weeks to 20 September even as Ituri fell 26% and Haut-Uélé fell 15%, which responders and outside experts attribute to weaker treatment access rather than a change in virus behavior; North Kivu's crude provincial CFR (~59.7%, 884/1,480) sits well above the national rate. A 23 September UN News report said one in three new cases nationally is still identified only after the patient has died outside a treatment center — a proxy for gaps in case detection and treatment access, echoing Africa CDC's 17 September finding that roughly 60% of reported deaths occur in communities rather than health facilities. Children under five face a markedly worse CFR, above 60%, versus roughly 40% among adults. Africa CDC warned 22 August that if the official case count captures only 30-40% of true infections, the true CFR could be substantially lower than the crude reported figure. BDBV historically 25–47% CFR; this outbreak's crude national CFR now sits at or above the top of the historical range.

label: BDBV Vaccine Status — Phase 3 Trial Now Underway in Ituri; 3,771+ Vaccinated Under Compassionate Use
value: Phase 3 Ervebo trial announced 'underway' by WHO 21 September, drawing on 20,000 of the 70,000 allocated doses; 3,771+ doses administered under compassionate use nationally (3,063 Tshopo, 708 Bas-Uélé) as of the 17 September DRC report; compassionate-use campaign expanded to Bunia and Mongbwalu, Ituri (the epicenter) 19 September alongside MSF/Epicentre's 20,000-person BRAVO effectiveness study
source: UN News (WHO) / MSF / Xinhua wire — 19-21 September 2026
contestNote: 20 August: WHO and Africa CDC announced the ICG approved immediate release of 70,000 Ervebo (rVSV-ZEBOV) doses to DRC — 20,000 for a Phase 3 clinical trial testing cross-protection against Bundibugyo virus, 50,000 for frontline and health workers. The compassionate-use campaign DRC launched 27 August reached Kisangani (Tshopo) and 14 health zones across three provinces in August before expanding to Bunia and Mongbwalu, Ituri — the outbreak epicenter — on 19 September; a Xinhua wire report the same weekend put the compassionate-use tally at 3,771 doses administered nationally, including 3,063 in Tshopo and 708 in Bas-Uélé. The same day, MSF and Epicentre launched BRAVO (Bundibugyo, Répondre Avec la Vaccination) with DRC's Ministry of Health, Africa CDC and INRB, an effectiveness study following up to 20,000 frontline workers for nine to 12 months. Congolese task force official Steve Ahuka cautioned 'we don't know to what degree it might be effective against the Bundibugyo strain,' since Ervebo was developed against Zaire ebolavirus. WHO announced 21 September that the separate Phase 3 randomized clinical trial — testing Ervebo's cross-protection against Bundibugyo virus, using 20,000 of the 70,000 allocated doses — is now underway in Ituri, stressing that community engagement remains key to controlling the outbreak. Two additional candidates (Oxford's ChAdOx1 BDBV in the UK and a Moderna mRNA candidate in Canada) remain in earlier-stage safety trials.
delta: WHO announced 21 September that the Phase 3 Ervebo trial is now underway in Ituri, following the 19 September epicenter vaccination expansion and BRAVO study launch
deltaNote: The 28 May WHO expert panel ruling barred Ervebo use outside research settings; the 7 August TAG-CVP recommendation, 12 August trial talks, 20 August dose allocation, 27 August compassionate-use campaign launch, 19 September epicenter expansion/BRAVO launch, and 21 September Phase 3 trial start are successive steps toward a structured clinical trial pathway alongside expanding frontline-worker protection. Since the ICG mechanism's 2021 establishment, over 56,000 Ervebo doses have been allocated for DRC outbreaks combined, plus 167,000 doses in preventive campaigns across five countries.

label: DRC Provinces + Countries Affected
value: 63 of 167 health zones across 7 DRC provinces + Uganda (outbreak closed) + France (recovered) + Germany (treated)
source: ECDC Ebola Outbreak Tracker (data as of 23 September) — published 25 September 2026
delta: Health-zone count held at 63 of 167 across all seven provinces (Ituri 6,032 cases/2,764 deaths across 28/36 zones, North Kivu 1,480/884 across 16/34, Haut-Uélé 322/130 across 7/13, Tshopo 43/15 across 7/23, Bas-Uélé 8/4 across 3/11, South Kivu 3/1 across 1/34, Sud-Ubangi 2/1 across 1/16); Africa CDC's Emergency Consultative Group said 17 September the data 'do not yet confirm that the outbreak has reached its peak,' disputing DRC Health Minister Roger Samuel Kamba's claim that growth had already peaked in mid-August
deltaNote: Ituri Province remains the epicenter with the large majority of cases and deaths across 28 of 36 health zones. North Kivu (16 of 34 zones, including Katwa, Biena and Manguredjipa) has the highest fatality rate of any affected province and continues to see rising transmission — cases there surged 73% over the three weeks to 20 September; officials link the acceleration to M23/government force fighting around Goma. Haut-Uélé, Tshopo, South Kivu and Bas-Uélé round out the six eastern provinces; Sud-Ubangi (first case 9 September, first in western DRC, bordering the Central African Republic and Republic of Congo) is now folded into the 167-zone denominator. Sud-Ubangi's acting governor Jean-René Galekwa Vundawe said 38 contacts of the index patient have been quarantined. Ebola cases were also detected among schoolchildren in Bunia, Ituri, as the 2026-27 school year opened in early September. Uganda's outbreak (Kampala + Wakiso) was declared over by its own Ministry of Health on 28 July and confirmed over by WHO on 25 August after the 42-day monitoring period. Mambasa Territory (IS-controlled) remains largely inaccessible to response teams. WHO's second IHR Emergency Committee meeting (24 August) maintained PHEIC status and expanded 'high risk' guidance to nine bordering states including Burundi and the Central African Republic. A US-convened G20+ Foreign Ministers' Meeting in New York on 23 September mobilized roughly $2.9 billion in cumulative international commitments toward the response.

label: Contact Tracing Coverage (DRC)
source: ECDC Ebola outbreak tracker — data as of 23 September 2026 (published 25 September)
delta: National coverage rebounded to 83.4% (23 September) from 79.9% (19 September)
deltaNote: The 23 September ECDC-reported data put active follow-up at 83.4% of identified contacts nationally, a partial rebound after the prior update's sharp drop. WHO's 100-day assessment noted tracing coverage had climbed dramatically from just 9% in the outbreak's first week, but the metric has fluctuated week to week (85.7% on 5 Sept → 88.3% on 7 Sept → 84.4% on 9 Sept → 88% on 12 Sept → 78.6% on 13 Sept → 87.6% on 16 Sept → 87.2% on 17 Sept → 79.9% on 19 Sept → 83.4% on 23 Sept). Africa CDC's Emergency Consultative Group cautioned 17 September that high reported contact-tracing percentages may mask gaps in initial contact identification. A recalibrated Lancet Infectious Diseases modelling study put the probability of Ebola spillover into South Sudan at roughly 69.3%, prompting a WHO/UNMISS preparedness mission to the border town of Ezo (27-28 August); no confirmed South Sudan case has been reported as of 23 September. Uganda's contact-tracing program is closed following its outbreak-end declaration, confirmed by WHO on 25 August. Mambasa Territory (IS-controlled) remains a contact-tracing dead zone, and community resistance (isolation refusals, a patient escape in Katwa, blocked ring-closure in Tshopo) is separately undermining follow-up in several provinces.
